"The immediate enactment of a Law on Internal Affairs ... immediate change of signs as well as the dismissal of all employees who have shown in their work that they are the destroyers of Yugoslavia ... JNA top command not to disband the Banja Luka Corps, arrest of war profiteers and the publication of names ... the dismissal of staff in the Jugobank in Banja Luka, the Privredna Bank, and Banja Luka Bank in order to prevent a monetary strike. We demand the dismissal in the post office where there are managerial staff who voted against Yugoslavia." The managerial staff who voted against Yugoslavia, in reality, did that mean those who had voted in the -- the referendum on whether Bosnia should be independent?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I heard you, Madam Prosecutor, but I did not really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. "We demand the dismissal of staff in the post office where there are managerial staff who voted against Yugoslavia ..." Does that mean managerial staff who voted in the referendum for Bosnia to be independent?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I really apologise, but I don't understand what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. The euphemism, there are managerial staff who voted against Yugoslavia, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't understand your inference. How would the managerial board vote? You vote at a referendum, not at the board. Something wrong with the proposition.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If there was a manager in the post office or in the Jugobank, or in the Privredna bank, who had voted in the referendum which Serbs by and large did not vote in, for Bosnia to become independent, is that what this demand refers to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, how are you supposed to establish or identify who voted how?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking if the reality, because you've lived in Banja Luka most of -- well, worked in Banja Luka most of your life, is it the people they were demanding should be sacked were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: They were not all Bosniaks. I know personally in the Banja Luka Bank that Goran Pegan was the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did he remain at the bank?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, he did for a while, and then he was replaced. The managerial board decided about staffing and replacements.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But looking at this list of demands, they were all political demands, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, there are unreasonable demands here. The demand to enforce the Law on Internal Affairs. Of course, we're going enforce the Law on Internal Affairs. They were asking us to do something which is our legal obligation that we are doing already, nor can anybody prevent us from enforcing the law. I just don't see the reason for putting this demand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That wasn't quite the question I asked. Would you describe these demands that were made by this gang of armed men as political ones?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, I would say these were the demands of people who turned up there. Somebody drafted them for them, and among them, there are unreasonable demand, in my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then at the end of the statement - sorry, we need go to the next page in English - thank you. No, that's not right. Should be page 3. Yeah, thank you. At the end of the statement, amongst other things, the SOS says: "We guarantee the complete safety of all Croats and Muslims and request them to refrain from provocation." What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, they seem to be placing themselves above the law, above the authorities. They can't guarantee anyone's security. It's the security forces who guarantee people's security.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Which is we started originally with this line of questioning. But what does "request them to refrain from provocation" mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, this negotiation takes place, and within a matter of hours, isn't that right, the -- all these -- what you call unreasonable, some of which are unreasonable demands, are accepted, are they not, by Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know what was accepted and what kind of negotiations they were. I didn't take part in the negotiations or the follow-up talks, because they invited me only for ten minutes, when I was asked to do something specifically. But how the process of negotiation went, I really don't know, and how the demands were formulated. I didn't take part in any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it -- but we can see, can't we, from this article that and, indeed, when we get to the press conference we will see that your name is mentioned. But within hours, this is -- the 3rd of April, and on the same day these demands have been accepted. Did that surprise you at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I should like to go back to the conclusions to be reminded what the conclusions were. The very fact that there were any surprises me, let alone everything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Can you imagine somebody putting a gun to your face and ... would you be surprised?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's have a look -- well, I don't know what you're saying there, Mr. Tutus. But when I say "weren't you surprised," weren't you surprised that nobody even discussed overpowering this illegal group of men who were taking over the streets?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I am telling you that, at the time, the use of force against those people by the security services was not an option that was considered. It would have been the beginning of a civilian -- of a civil war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why? These were -- their announcement said that these were Serbs. Why would it have been a civil war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, you don't have to have people of different ethnicity in order to have a civil war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's have a look, please, at the -- at the demands which were -- what was accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Page 4 in English, and it's the second page in the B/C/S. You can find that, I think. It's the top left-hand side. No, I think you need to move it to the B/C/S to the right, slightly. Well, before we move it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the top picture, do we see -- who do we see there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I can recognise President Radic. It's not very clear. Could it be enlarged, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The photograph on the top right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see President Radic. I can also see Brdjanin. I think this person here is Dr. Vukic. And as for the person to the left, or, rather, to the right, to Radic's right, I can't recognise him. It's a little obscure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So Radic. We can see, I think, Brdjanin in the white shirt?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the person furthest right, as we look at the photograph, is Vukic. And then President Radic is next to Brdjanin, on the other side. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's look at the demands. Sorry, the acceptance of the demands.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the left site of this newspaper article. Yeah. Just there. And if we go -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that -- can you see the part -- I hope this is the right part. The law that the -- the resolutions which were accepted or the demands, the Law on Internal Affairs will be fully enacted. In order to keep their jobs, all the current employees in the security service centre will have to sign what is called a statement of loyalty here. I think you have been through this. Whether it's called a statement of loyalty, or an oath of loyalty, or a solemn declaration, it's -- we're all talking about the same thing. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But the legal term is solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Apart from that, staff will be reorganised. People loyal to the Serbian Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be appointed to key position. The demand was also accepted to request the Presidency of the SFRY and the General Staff of the JNA to reinforce the Banja Luka Corps. And then tribute was paid to the soldiers and officers. Agreement also reached on the demand to start the prosecution of all war profiteers and thieves and to publish all criminal offences, blah blah. The Crisis Staff also passed a decision to dismiss the directors of the Banja Luka bank and the Jugobank by 6th of April, accepted the demand to dismiss all post office staff who had voted against Yugoslavia by the 10th of April. And so on and so forth. So, without any hesitation, the negotiations apparently have resulted in the acceptance of these demands. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that last part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The negotiations have resulted, it would seem, in complete capitulation to the SOS demands, including sacking people for no other reason than they voted against Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: If that's what it says in this article, well, there is nothing I can add. The person who compiled this, who wrote the article, well, I don't know anything about this. I didn't participate in the conclusions, and I don't know about the sources. I can just tell you about things I participated in, about the truth. But when it comes to assessing an article that appeared in a newspaper, I really don't think this is something I can do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, when you saw this article, as you told Mr. Sebire you did at the time, didn't you think of saying to anybody, How come they accepted all these demands?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I said anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at the second part of this article that I want to ask you about, which is the Crisis Staff, that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, as you move into the second part, would, this be a convenient point to take the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, still on the same article, can you go to that -- in the B/C/S, can we move that box in the middle page across slightly. It's headed: "Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, so we get -- no, we need to get the whole thing in, which it isn't at the moment. It's too big. And for, in English, we need to go to the, I don't know, sixth page. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It says: "In Banja Luka, after the blockade of the city and presentation of their demands by the SOS, a Crisis Staff was formed whose President is Predrag Radic, President of the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly. Predrag Mitrakovic is also on the staff on behalf of the Banja Luka municipality." Can you tell us who he was, Mr. Tutus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Predrag Mitrakovic was the secretary of the Secretariat for Urbanism and Utilities in the Municipal Assembly of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then: "... representing the Security Services Centre is its chief, Stojan Zupljanin, and then" -- you, "chief of the public security station." Now, was it discussed with you that you were going to be a member of this Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, when you saw the newspaper the next day and you saw your name as a member of the Crisis Staff, what did you do about it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Nothing. I attached absolutely no importance to the fact. No one ever appointed me through an official document to state organ of any kind. I thought that this was illegal. In my opinion it wasn't something I should really concern myself with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I understand that, Mr. Tutus. But on the face of it, the public were being told you were a member of the Crisis Staff. Did you speak to Mr. Radic or Mr. Zupljanin about it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't speak to Mr. Zupljanin about the subject. I went to meetings with President Radic, and I would attend those meetings for ten or 15 minutes. We never spoke about the conclusions, et cetera. Quite simply, I didn't take this to be a regular body that I should take into account, or with regard to which I should take decisions of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I'm just asking you, leave aside the other meetings you went to with Mr. Radic and I'll come on to those a little later, but when you -- you told us a moment ago that you never were consulted about this. Did you really not feel that you should say to somebody, Why does my name appear in the newspaper as a member of a body about which I know nothing?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I'll repeat what I said. I didn't ask anyone about this. I thought this was without any value. I wouldn't have achieved anything by acting in this way. This had been published and that was the end of the story.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on with the other members. Milorad Sajic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: He was the commander of the TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then Milos Kesic and Miroslav Vesic. They were apparently also connected with the TOs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then on behalf of the justice department, Mr. Puvacic and Jovo Rosic. Did you know both of them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then Colonel Kelecevic. What was his --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes, he was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Bogdan Subotic from the Banja Luka Corps. Is that the Subotic who became the minister of defence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then Dr. Vukic whom you identified in the photograph. And Nenad --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: He was the SDS president in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And Nenad Stevandic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: At the time, I knew him as a student of medicine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It says on "behalf of the political parties."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know on behalf of which political party he was present. I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Was there something called a Sokol Society in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: There was a Sokol Society. I'm not a historian, but I think it was at the time of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. This Sokol Society was dismantled, and then during this period of time it was re-animated. The Sokol Society came to life again. I know that the press wrote about it, Mandic was apparently at the head of that society.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Stevandic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Stevandic, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I'm sorry. Mr. Stevandic, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did Nenad Stevandic go on to work for the SNB in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then Radoslav Brdjanin represents the autonomous regions assembly, and the Serbian Defence Forces representatives are firstly Ilija Milinkovic. Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: At the time, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently discover?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Subsequently, I discovered that he worked in the company that was called Metal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Slobodan Popovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know that person, and I still don't know that person today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Aleksandar Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Similarly, I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ranko Dubocanin.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: The first time I saw him was when we were there on the first day, when I was with President Radic, then a person wearing glasses appeared. Later I asked who he was. They said that it was Slobodan Dubocanin's brother. That's how I know him, but I didn't really know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the same Slobodan Dubocanin who became part of the special police unit of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a member of the special police unit in Banja Luka, but I do know that he was in uniform and that he was a member of some sort of a military formation. I believe he wore camouflage unit [as interpreted] and I think he was a member of the Territorial Defence, but I'm not quite sure which unit he was engaged in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Was Slobodan Dubocanin somebody you knew personally?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally. But later on, as time passed by, he would appear on occasion. I asked about him, since he is from Banja Luka, and my wife told him that he was a year or two above her in school. That's all I know about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about him going to Kotor Varos during 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we look, please, at the next box in the B/C/S. It will have to go over a bit to the right -- move the document towards the left. Yeah, the box under the picture. No, no, the box under the picture of Brdjanin and all that. Yes, there, stop. Stop. Okay. Can we highlight that bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Is that headed "Peace in the Interests of all Three Nations"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it says: "They are replying to a reporter's question about what to do with the security services centre's employee who did not sign the statement of loyalty to the Serbian Republic ..." Again, they're calling it the statement of loyalty. "... by the 6th of April, Stojan Zupljanin briefly said, 'They will not be able to continue working.'" And was that something that you heard him say?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I didn't hear that, but I have read it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, finally, on this document, can we look, please, in the B/C/S at the third page, and in the English translation, on the ninth page. It's the box at the -- at the -- at the bottom left-hand side. So we need to -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "From hour to hour, the proclamation of the Serbian Defence Forces was read out over radio Banja Luka at 9.00 and the demands laid out in seven points. The President of the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly schedules the Crisis Staff session at 11.00."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then if we go to the next page in the English, at the bottom:

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "At 11.00, representatives of the SOS [sic] come to the municipality Assembly where they agreed positions with [sic] the Crisis Staff." So within a matter of a very few hours, according to this timetable, those demands were acceded to. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: If things are as stated here, then that was done a very few hours later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there's -- as a police officer of considerable experience and authority, you took no part in -- in any of these negotiations. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Thank you, that's all I want to ask on this document. Now before we move on, you say you weren't a member of this Crisis Staff that was set up to deal with the SOS. Were you, however, a member of what you called the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Of the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Predrag Radic the -- the President of this War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There was yourself. Can you recall who else was -- was -- was a member of this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were people who had positions in the town administration. I think the commander of the TO defence was also a member. I think that the district prosecutor and the President of the district court were members. As far as my memory serves me, I think that they were members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And the Municipal War Presidency was a different body from the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff, then War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: The War Presidency in Banja Luka municipality worked according to the statute. It had its legislative powers -- powers according to the legislation and rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: As for this War Presidency for the region, I don't know on the basis of which they worked, whether there were any regulations governing their work, what their competences were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But -- you were aware that there was such a thing, because, as we'll see later, Zupljanin mentioned it on a number of occasions, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: He may have mentioned it, but I can't recall all these details now. I read in the press that something like that exists. I can't say I didn't know that the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, can you tell us when exactly you were appointed a member of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1991, I was elected chief of the station, just after the multi-party elections, and, at that time, according to the statute of the municipality that body was called Council for National Defence, under the legislation prevailing at the time. Later, when the immediate threat of war was proclaimed, that I believe that was in 1992, that body was just renamed into War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Tutus. I was under the impression that the War Presidencies were the bodies that succeeded the Crisis Staffs. But am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are wrong. That wasn't so in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So did the Crisis Staff persist and remain in place in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, apart from what we were discussing today, and I don't think it's the same thing. If you wish me, I can repeat. In 1991, I received an appointment as member of the Council for National Defence, which was later renamed War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand and I did pick up your answer just a while ago. But tell us, what was the relation, then, between the War Presidency and -- and -- I was going to ask you what was the relation between the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff, but your answer is that there was no Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What were the functions of the War Presidencies in Banja Luka, while you were a member of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Remember, the War Presidency adopted some conclusions and decisions and reviewed the security situations. I, for instance, had the job of reporting to them about the security situation. Affairs which were urgent and had to deal with were decided upon by the War Presidency. However, these decisions were subject, ultimately, to verification by the Assembly, when the Assembly managed to meet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what I was going ask you next, you see. The War Presidency was supposed to exist only if the Assembly couldn't meet. But the Assembly continued to meet, didn't it, during 1992.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: You're right. The Assembly did meet. But I didn't convene Assembly meetings. I don't know if it was able to meet when they needed it to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking you about. You say that you would report on -- on -- to the War Presidency about the security situation and decisions were made by the War Presidency. But if the Assembly could meet, why weren't those decisions being taken by the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that under the documents of the Assembly, all these decisions had to be verified by the Assembly. I don't know why they did not convene the Assembly instead of the War Presidency. But whenever I was required to brief or report to the War Presidency, or the Assembly, or whatever, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I understand that. But what I'm asking you is whether you are able to assist us as to whether, as I am asking you about, the Assembly itself was actually continuing to meet during 1992 when this so-called War Presidency was also meeting. If you don't know the answer, then say so.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I know that the Assembly, for the most part, operated. For a short while, there were no meetings. In fact, there were few meetings of the War Presidency. I don't know why they did not convene the Assembly instead of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was it the -- could the War Presidency -- could Mr. Radic, as the President of the War Presidency, give orders to you as -- as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: No, he could not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, you told us that you didn't pay any attention to your membership of the Crisis Staff. You have more or less said the Crisis Staff didn't really exist. We saw that Mr. Zupljanin was your chief. Did -- was also a member of this Crisis Staff. Do I take it, then, that he considered as, well -- considered as well that this -- that Crisis Staff and its membership was of no importance at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot say this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all that I want to ask you about that. Let move on to a different matter. Let us start on the topic of the special police. Can you have a look, please, at, first of all, document number 99. Yeah, 65 ter 99.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this document is signed and stamped by Vojo Kupresanin. You knew who Vojo Kupresanin was, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's a decision of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, dated the 27th of April, on the formation of a special purpose police detachment which is to be formed within the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. And then it sets out how many people, and then up. Did you become aware of this decision made by the Assembly of the Autonomous Region.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So at no stage, because, as you know, the special police detachment was formed, did -- were you ever told that -- by Zupljanin that this was as a result of the Assembly decision?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I don't think so. We didn't even discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we look then next, please, at P552. Now, that's an article in Glas, two days after this decision. And I think it's the one that is -- is it -- in the middle of the page. That one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does that say: "Special detachments to be formed soon"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. And it's an interview with Stojan Zupljanin. And what he says is that the primary function of the special detachment to be formed within the security service --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if a -- for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- for the benefit of the witness, if the document can be taken down on the Serbian, because it shows the different article from the one that you are citing right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh I see, it's the one above -- yes, sorry, it's the one below.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, it's the one below.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. sorry, you're quite right. Thank you. And have you to move across slightly. So you have to just shrink it slightly so you can see the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "'The primary function of the special detachment to be formed within the Security Service Centre, in accordance with the decision brought forward [sic] yesterday by the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina will be anti-sabotage and anti-terrorist combat,' stated Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the Banja Luka CSB." And then it goes on to say that -- as to the Serbian Defence Forces, SOS, which were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre by the Krajina Assembly decisions, Zupljanin said that a large number of these units members, being reliable and experienced fighters, would be tested for engagement in the special detachment whilst other -- others would be assigned to the reserve police force." And did you read this article?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: The last part you read, where is it? Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: About the SOS?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, did you read this article at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I probably did. I can't remember all the things I read 15 years ago. But I suppose I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you read Glas on a regular basis at that period?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there, it said, according to Zupljanin, this is being formed as a result of the decision yesterday by the Assembly. Which you said you hadn't realised. Does it -- does this now remind you that you did know that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I didn't know. Although this was published. But I can't really say I read it on the same day. But I'm not questioning anything here. If the press published it this way, I -- there's no reason for me to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then it says -- it talks about the SOS having been placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre. Now, given that you were in the same building as the CSB, were you aware that the SOS had now been placed under the jurisdiction of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I did not know that the SOS was placed under the jurisdiction of the CSB, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: And I can't find this sentence that you read. I -- I just can't find it in the article.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to have to ask for the assistance of one of the Defence counsel, because I don't know where it is either.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I can see one sentence here, which says: "In this way, the SOS, S will practically disappear."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It's the last paragraph in the first column on the left in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the sentence: "SOS will practically cease to exist."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, it's the last sentence -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to have to ask for assistance. Do the words, as put in English, "As to the Serbian Defence Forces which were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre by the Krajina Assembly decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may of any assistance, it would appear that this is the last paragraph of the -- of the -- of the previous -- on the left side. The last paragraph on the left side of this framed -- framed article.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: It says Zupljanin says that a large number of members of these units will be tested. And then it moves to the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, quite, but the -- no, no, can we stay where we are, please. Thank you. What I'm asking you about is the article says that the SOS were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, I can't find it in the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, this is for the nth time what I have been asking, somebody, if they can help. Is it not the first line of that last paragraph on that page? Which -- if you read that first sentence, under the word "Zupljanin," which we can see in heavy type, does that not say: "As to the Serbian Defence Forces, which were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre ..."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes, but there is a sentence after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I -- look, Mr. Tutus, we're getting a bit buried here. All I want to know is are you telling the Court that, until you saw this article, but you saw it because you're not sure, you did not know that the SOS was now under the jurisdiction of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you known this, what, if anything, would you have done?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't believe it. I wouldn't have believed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: It doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Why doesn't it make sense?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: First of all, it doesn't make sense that the Assembly of the Autonomous Region Krajina establishes police units. Police units may be set up only by the minister of interior, in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs. Now, for the SOS to be placed under the control of the CSB, it says under that jurisdiction, that is something I could not believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's what I'm asking you. Why?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, it's not lawful.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that's the only reason that you couldn't believe that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: It's not in keeping with the law and it's not in conformity with the procedure. It's impossible to admit that entire unit into the CSB. I just can't accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. What about the fact that -- except if this is correct, and this is what Zupljanin is apparently saying to the newspaper, these men, the SOS, were people who had behaved illegally by setting up barricades and threatening people. Is that something that might worry you, if they were taken into the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, I simply can't accept that anyone who had been prosecuted or had a criminal record or charges filed against them could be admitted into the Security Services. It's simply not in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But do you mean that you were aware that some of the members of the SOS had criminal records?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: My associates informed me when I arrived at work that day that there were people among that group who were known to the police as having been convicted before and people prone to crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And those people who your associates recognised should never have been allowed to become part of the CSB. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, people with criminal records cannot be admitted under the law into the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were any of the other people, to your knowledge, who had erected the barricades and -- and threatened people, were they ever prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, information reached me from the CID that there were people among them, people among those on the barricades, who had been prosecuted before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. But do you agree that what happened in Banja Luka on the 3rd of April, by these barricades being put up and these armed men being in the streets, was an illegal activity?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, it certainly doesn't fit into the prevailing legislation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That, I think, is an understatement. But -- however, would you have expected that people who had behaved like this would be prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: We prosecuted them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: The public security station Banja Luka documented all the criminal acts by SOS members and filed reports with the competent prosecutor's offices.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure, this is the SOS as opposed to the special police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about the SOS and the special police, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to what this article says. From what you're saying, what Zupljanin says about these people "being reliable and experienced fighters who would be tested for engagement in the special detachment," you found, to say the at least, to be a remarkable statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: It's possible that he had some information about individuals or groups or larger groups who had been to war before. There was a war in Croatia, and maybe they had experience from that theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, well, that's all I want to ask you about that particular article.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry is it not an exhibit? No. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What's the number? I've lost track of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was P --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I know. Yes, I know. Thank you. The numbering is so askew ... all right, yes. Can we look, please, at document 111, 65 ter 111.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is addressed to -- it's from the General Trade Association of Small Businessmen in Banja Luka. It's addressed to the municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we turn over to the second page in both the English and B/C/S. Yeah, can we look at -- exactly. Can we look at the -- to whom it was delivered? Delivered --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Firstly did you know the gentleman who signed it, Mr. Kulenovic and Mr. Slavko Prosan?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Kulenovic, I think I know him if it's the Kulenovic who was the director of a metallurgy school in Banja Luka. But as for the other person, no, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And one -- it's addressed -- delivered to, rather, from the addressee which is the municipal Crisis Staff. The executive council of the autonomous region. The president of the association of the municipality, the executive council, and chief of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre and chief of the municipal public security stations. Now, does that mean that you would have got this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't remember the document, but perhaps I did receive it. But here it says to the heads of the SJBs, so it was addressed to number of municipalities. That's how I interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. But would you have been one of them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go back to the front -- the first page on each. It's a complaint about -- what it says in the third paragraph, extortion, vandalism, and the fact that it's increased and it's becoming more brutal. Now, did you do anything about these complaints?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I can't remember individual cases. It is true that there were such occurrences in the territory of the Banja Luka SJB, and we took certain measures. We shed light on cases, filed reports, arrested individuals. I'd probably forward this to the crime service for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The real question I want to ask you about this in the light of your answers. You say you don't know anything about a municipal Crisis Staff, just a municipal War Presidency. But a month later, this association is addressing this document to the municipal Crisis Staff. Now, I -- going back to Judge Harhoff's questions, wasn't it -- in this early part of 1992, wasn't the War Presidency in fact the Crisis Staff, which later became the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: As far as I understand matters, the Crisis Staff in Banja Luka didn't exist. There was no such staff. Someone might have used one name or a different name for it. But far as I know, there was no Crisis Staff in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the light of the fact that he accepts that it was addressed to him, he almost certainly received it, may I ask that this be marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1079, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we now then move, please -- later on that month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, could I ask a question. Mr. Tutus - thank you - are you familiar -- you are familiar, of course, with the term "Crisis Staff" being used other than in Banja Luka when you say it didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm familiar with the term "Crisis Staff" and the term was used in certain municipalities. I'm familiar with that term. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I'll try and -- is it possible that, in general usage of the term, that the word "Crisis Staff" was applied to a variety -- to arrangements such as you say existed in Banja Luka as a sort of generic or general term? Is that a possibility, in terms of general usage by other persons? If you didn't understand my question, I will try and rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: What I'm trying to get an understanding of is putting the answers that you would were previously given, especially the answers that you gave to Judge Harhoff a while ago, in terms of the impression that we have developed so far, and I'm only asking this, whether generally speaking, the word "Crisis Staff" may have come to be used as a sort of a catch-all phrase to -- to encompass even the type of arrangement that you say existed in Banja Luka. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the War Presidency in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No. I am thinking of the -- what pre-dated the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be quite frank, I haven't understood you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'll let you go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I -- I can try one more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think what you're being asked, Mr. Tutus, is this. You call the body to which you belonged and to which Mr. Radic was the president the War Presidency. Is it possible that the general public believed it to be called the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I would sooner say that the Crisis Staff of the Krajina region headed by Brdjanin -- well, I'd say that the public thought that was the Crisis Staff. As far as I know, the public at large didn't think that the Banja Luka municipality had a Crisis Staff. I think that they had in mind the Crisis Staff headed by Brdjanin. The Crisis Staff of which Brdjanin was the president. He tended to appear more frequently in public, so I think that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you've -- but -- so you've no explanation as to why this group of shopkeepers was addressing this document to the municipal Crisis Staff, as opposed to the regional Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I have no explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We're moving to the 13th of May, when the -- there was this parade in Banja Luka of the police. Were you, did you attend the parade as an observer?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I was present with my wife. I was quite simply there amongst the citizens.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In a moment, I will ask you to watch the video which had you a chance to watch before. Was Mico Stanisic also present at that parade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask to you watch it and we may stop it from time to time. I have forgotten what the number is now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we just pause for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: These vehicles, were these normal police vehicles or were they specific to the special police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: These are military vehicles, in my opinion. They're used by the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But are they being, in fact, driven by people in police uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: But I assume that it's the police, although I can't see the uniforms. It looks like a military uniform to me, a blue one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, who wore a blue military uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, the police would wear blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: We can see some men in blue camouflage uniforms. At least that's my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And those -- are those blue camouflage uniforms, again, police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The helicopters. Were there police helicopters in Banja Luka at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I know there were helicopters, but as to whose they were, I don't know. Banja Luka had a helicopter before the war. And immediately prior to the war, it was taken to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was this the first -- when you were watching there, was this the first time that you'd seen then helicopters?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: No. How could it be the first time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was a bad question. What I mean is -- I didn't mean have you ever seen a helicopter before. Was this the first time you'd seen, apparently, helicopters back as part of the police armaments, as it were, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I was present. I was amongst the citizens down there, and I know that these helicopters were flying over. I think they had some sort of signs. But as for whether they were police helicopters or military helicopters or anything of that sort, I don't know. I didn't even wonder about that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But this was an entirely police parade, wasn't it, not a military -- not a combined parade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I don't know to whom those helicopters belonged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Are these also police forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And these, police as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And a rather undisciplined lot of police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we see where you were standing? Oh, we've now moved off.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on. Let's go on now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is your viewpoint shown anywhere in this video that we've seen so far?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I know where I was standing. It was in front of the post office, at the cross-roads between the park and Petar Kostic Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the people who were taking part in this parade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Yes, there are some people I recognised there. My policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who is that taking the salute in the green camouflage?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to recognise someone from behind. But he's saluting the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can all see that. Are you able to -- did you watch this part where the salute was going on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: Well, I probably did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, who took the salute? Who's that, in the green camouflage?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: I'm telling you, it's difficult to recognise someone from behind. But I can tell you who I think he is. It's an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You tell us who you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS
utterances.text: But I can't claim for certain, since I can only see him from behind. I think it's Minister Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, if you ask me, I'd say that was a fairly good guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we just finish this off.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Your Honours, that may be an appropriate moment. And may I ask that this now be -- I don't think we've had it admitted and marked so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1080, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, just while we have this in our fresh minds, what was -- Mr. Tutus, actually, I put my question to you. What was the occasion of this parade. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The parade was held for the day of security services in the former Yugoslavia. We celebrate at the 13th of May as the day of the security services. I think this was on the 14th, perhaps, but the reason for this parade was to celebrate the Security Services Day. All police forces participated in the parade. There were members of various services, there was the traffic police, the general police, and so on and so forth. So the reason was to celebrate the Security Services Day, and this day was celebrated every year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So Police Day, it was. Was that throughout the former Yugoslavia or was it only in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout Yugoslavia. The Security Services Day was celebrated throughout Yugoslavia and there was certain sports activities that also took place to celebrate this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One last small correction, Mr. Tutus. I'm coming back to the helicopters. Supposingly there are police -- if we suppose there are police helicopters, did you know that public service or that the security services had helicopters in Banja Luka before? Did you know that, or is it something new?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that the Banja Luka SUP had helicopters. I personally used the helicopter to go from Banja Luka to Sarajevo. It was a Gazelle bought in France. We had our own heliport. We had a hanger for helicopters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, we are about to take the adjournment for the day. You, having been sworn as a witness, you cannot have any communication with counsel from either side in this matter, and in such conversations as you may have with persons outside of the courtroom, you cannot discuss your testimony. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand and that's how I shall proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment now, to reconvene in Courtroom III tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
